speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing fatigue, severe itching, and abnormal liver function; to determine the underlying cause, please describe your age, sex, and any recent travel or medication use. Also, have you noticed any jaundice, dark urine, or pale stools?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC). The patient's presentation of severe pruritus, fatigue, and abnormal liver enzymes in a young female (despite the input stating 'male', the clinical picture of PBC is overwhelmingly associated with females) with a history of autoimmune conditions like ulcerative colitis is highly suggestive. However, the mention of sexual activity with multiple partners and inconsistent condom use raises concern for viral hepatitis or HIV coinfection which can also cause pruritus and liver dysfunction. I will proceed with specific serologic testing to differentiate between an autoimmune etiology and an infectious one. REQUEST TEST: Anti-Mitochondrial Antibody (AMA), Hepatitis B surface antigen, Hepatitis C antibody, and HIV antigen/antibody. REQUEST TEST: Serum alkaline phosphatase, bilirubin, AST, ALT. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal ultrasound.
